## Second instance, found the same day — this is a class, not an incident

objectui#8044's dev hit the identical shape while landing PR #8669 and reported it rather than fixing it:

**`.changeset/core-datascope-field-and-comparison-guards-7751.md`** states, in the present tense, that `@object-ui/permissions`' `evaluateCondition` still returns `true` for `{ field: 'toString', operator: 'neq' }`.

**PR #8669 makes that false.** It is the fix for exactly that read. If both ship in one release, the changeset publishes the superseded sentence **verbatim to the CHANGELOG**, describing a fail-open that the same release closes.

## Why the dev was right to leave it alone

⛔ It is **another card's release note** (objectui#7751's), and release notes are written centrally at release time — never accreted or amended by a rider on an unrelated code PR. Rewriting it from PR #8669 would have been the wrong remedy in the same way this card says the first instance's would be.

⇒ Flagged in the PR body for the release editor, and recorded here so the two instances sit under one heading.

## What the two instances have in common — and it is the actionable part

Both are **an unreleased changeset asserting a present-tense fact about code that a LATER, SEPARATE PR then changes.** Neither author did anything wrong: the sentence was true when written, it is load-bearing (it is the justification for the change it accompanies), and nothing re-reads a pending changeset when a subsequent PR falsifies it.

⇒ the gap is that **`.changeset/*.md` is write-once in practice and unread until publish**, so the window between "written" and "published" is unguarded — and it is precisely the window in which a fast-moving queue lands the contradicting fix. Two instances in one day on a queue running three agents is the rate this produces.

Worth stating for whoever grades this: the remedy is unlikely to be "check changesets for stale claims" (nothing can know which future PR falsifies which sentence). The tractable version is narrower — **a changeset that asserts current behaviour of a package it does not itself change** is the shape that rots, and that one is mechanically detectable.

⇒ live, two days after filing. Control: the same listing returns **1327** pending changesets, so the directory is being read and the two hits are readings.

### ⚠️ This class has already cost once, in the sibling repo — the deadline is not hypothetical

objectstack#16859 is the same shape and its window **closed**: the changeset was consumed and the false statement is now frozen in `packages/spec/CHANGELOG.md:3407`, unfixable. That card is currently reported to the maintainer precisely because nothing can be done about it any more. ⇒ this is what happens to this card if it waits for a release, and it is why p1 is about time rather than blast radius.

### Both instances are one dispatch — the fold is deliberate

Comment 5591915287 records a second instance found the same day (`core-datascope-field-and-comparison-guards-7751.md`, a present-tense claim about `@object-ui/per…`). Same defect shape, same repair, same directory, one changeset, one queue slot, and each is independently checkable by reading its own file. ⇒ folded into this card.

⛔ **Excluded from the fold, named so the boundary is explicit:** any *other* pending changeset whose prose merely reads oddly, and every changeset whose claim is still true. This card covers **exactly the two files named above**. A third instance is a new reading and gets re-measured, ⛔ not assumed.

### ⭐ The constraint the implementing seat identified is upheld, ⛔ not overridden

PR #8615's seat declined to fix the file in passing, reasoning that an unreleased changeset is owned by the release pipeline and the in-place-fix exemption's *"no other claim holds that file"* condition could not be verified from inside that PR. **That was correct** and it is why this card exists: this card is the claim on those files. The dev taking it now holds them and may edit them.

⚠️ And the seat's own mitigation is correctly judged insufficient by the card: PR #8615's changeset states the corrected fact in the **same CHANGELOG section**, so leaving the stale one produces a section asserting both *"the spec and the table agree on this key"* and *"the table disagreed, so we flipped it"*, with no way for a reader to tell which is current. ⇒ two contradictory sentences in one section is a worse artifact than one stale sentence. Correcting is not optional.

### Scope

Correct the prose in the two named files so each states what is true today. ⛔ Do not change either changeset's **bump level** — that re-prices a release and is not this card's call. ⛔ Do not delete either changeset: both describe real shipped changes that owe a CHANGELOG entry.

⚠️ **Do not treat a green gate as evidence here.** Nothing in this repository parses changeset prose for truth, so every gate will stay green whether this is fixed or not. The acceptance evidence is the corrected text read back from the file, plus the two `git ls-tree` probes above.

`Size/model suggestion:` S, mechanical on the edit — but it needs a careful reader, because the deliverable is a factual claim about what the installed spec does today, not a code change. Verify the current fact (`ApprovalEscalationSchema.safeParse({ timeoutHours: 24 })` on installed 17.3.0) before rewriting the sentence rather than copying this card's account of it.

⚠️ **Reported to the maintainer in this round's report** as a time-limited item: PM seats never run releases, so if a release fires before this lands, the window closes exactly as objectstack#16859's did.

`origin/main` = `4d65991c5`, **tip committed 2026-09-10T15:31:10Z**; head `134077605`, **committed 16:02:36Z**. Two files, **+7 / −4**, prose only. No model identifier in the commits.

### ⭐ Two places the dev refused to do what it was told, and was right both times

**1. This card says both clauses in instance one are false. Measurement says one is.** 「installed spec and table agree on it today」 is **still true**: the spec returns `enabled: true` **and** the table declares `'true'` after PR objectui#8615 flipped it. ⇒ kept **verbatim**, per the dispatch's own instruction that a sentence which turns out to be true is reported rather than edited. ⭐ The pair went false when the spec bumped and true again when #8615 landed; only the false tense **around** that clause was repaired.

**2. It corrected the card's version fact.** Installed `@objectstack/spec` is **17.4.0**, ⛔ not the 17.3.0 the card states.

⚠️ ⭐ **And this seat nearly sent it back over that number.** A first read of `pnpm-lock.yaml` returned 17.2.0 and looked like a contradiction — because that read went through the **shared checkout's working tree** instead of `git show origin/main:…`. Re-run against `origin/main`, **17.4.0 is the only version string in that file** and every importer resolves to it. ⇒ the dev's measurement stands and this seat's did not. ⛔ Same shape as this seat's earlier stale-ref error, in a new dress; recorded as errata 12.

Line 9 still reads 「the installed `@objectstack/spec` (17.2.0)」 while installed is 17.4.0, and the dev chose to leave it. ⭐ **Correct**, and this seat checked by reading the sentence rather than the question: its governing verb is 「**declared**」 — past tense. The whole clause is a record of the state the change addressed, so `(17.2.0)` is the version that **was** installed when it was measured. ⇒ rewriting it to today's version would make the record **false**, ⛔ not true. ⛔ Scope held: no bump level moved (the overwrite gate reads both back unchanged), neither changeset deleted, no other changeset touched, ⛔ no release note written or re-framed, ⛔ no gate built for the structural half.
